---
title: "PRDC notes"
---

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
source("R/book.R")
```

QuantLib has no PRDC instrument. But in this model each coupon is a floor plus a call spread on the FX rate, so a reference can be built from QuantLib's `blackFormula`. The legacy text has only Monte Carlo values, so this chapter has no verdicts.

## Inputs

```{r}
#| label: inputs
valuation_date <- "2023-04-11"
terms <- list(
  effective = "2015-09-03", termination = "2041-09-03", notional = 3e8, spot = 133.2681, volatility = 0.10,
  domestic_rate = 0.01, foreign_rate = 0.03, discount_rate = 0.005,
  fx_base = 120, leverage = 0.122, subtraction = 0.10, floor = 0, cap = 0.022
)
show_inputs(c(list(valuation = valuation_date), terms, list(schedule = "6M, TARGET, modified following, backward", day_count = "Actual/360")))
```

The note is discounted at 0.5%, while the FX drift is 1% - 3%. `prdc_value` takes one domestic curve for both purposes. The same model is reached with a domestic curve at 0.5% and a foreign curve at 2.5%, which keep the drift at -2%. This is a change of inputs, and not a separate discount curve; see @sec-gaps.

```{r}
#| label: dates
schedule <- QuantLib::Schedule(
  ql_date(terms$effective), ql_date(terms$termination), QuantLib::Period(6L, "Months"), QuantLib::TARGET(),
  "ModifiedFollowing", "ModifiedFollowing", "Backward", FALSE
)
schedule_dates <- map(seq_len(QuantLib::Schedule_size(schedule)) - 1L, \(i) ql_iso(QuantLib::Schedule_date(schedule, i))) |> list_c()
position <- which(schedule_dates > as.Date(valuation_date))
coupon_dates <- schedule_dates[position]
times <- as.numeric(coupon_dates - as.Date(valuation_date)) / 360
accruals <- as.numeric(coupon_dates - schedule_dates[position - 1L]) / 360
drift <- terms$domestic_rate - terms$foreign_rate
domestic_curve_rate <- terms$discount_rate
foreign_curve_rate <- terms$discount_rate - drift
show_inputs(list(coupons = length(times), first_coupon = coupon_dates[1], last_coupon = max(coupon_dates), domestic_curve = domestic_curve_rate, foreign_curve = foreign_curve_rate))
```

RiemannFinMath has no public schedule, so both sides take the dates above from QuantLib.

## Closed form

Baseline on `blackFormula`:

```{r}
#| label: baseline
baseline_npv <- function(spot = terms$spot, volatility = terms$volatility, discount = domestic_curve_rate, foreign = foreign_curve_rate) {
  forwards <- spot * exp((discount - foreign) * times)
  deviations <- volatility * sqrt(times)
  low <- terms$fx_base * (terms$subtraction + terms$floor) / terms$leverage
  high <- terms$fx_base * (terms$subtraction + terms$cap) / terms$leverage
  call_on <- function(strike) {
    map2_dbl(forwards, deviations, \(f, d) QuantLib::blackFormula(QuantLib::Option_Call_get(), strike, f, d, 1))
  }
  rates <- terms$floor + terms$leverage / terms$fx_base * (call_on(low) - call_on(high))
  discounts <- exp(-discount * times)
  terms$notional * (sum(accruals * rates * discounts) + discounts[length(discounts)])
}
# The vega is a formula here: a finite difference on this notional has an error above the tolerance.
baseline_vega <- function() {
  forwards <- terms$spot * exp((domestic_curve_rate - foreign_curve_rate) * times)
  deviations <- terms$volatility * sqrt(times)
  low <- terms$fx_base * (terms$subtraction + terms$floor) / terms$leverage
  high <- terms$fx_base * (terms$subtraction + terms$cap) / terms$leverage
  black_vega <- function(strike) forwards * dnorm(log(forwards / strike) / deviations + deviations / 2) * sqrt(times)
  terms$notional * sum(accruals * exp(-domestic_curve_rate * times) * terms$leverage / terms$fx_base * (black_vega(low) - black_vega(high)))
}
```

RiemannFinMath:

```{r}
#| label: riemann
domestic <- flat_curve(valuation_date, domestic_curve_rate, "actual_360", "tonar")
foreign <- flat_curve(valuation_date, foreign_curve_rate, "actual_360", "sofr")
riemann_note <- function(spot = terms$spot, volatility = terms$volatility, ...) {
  RiemannFinMath::prdc_value(
    spot, volatility, domestic, foreign, times, accruals, terms$fx_base, terms$leverage, terms$subtraction,
    terms$floor, terms$cap, notional = terms$notional, ...
  )
}
closed <- riemann_note()
```

```{r}
#| label: closed-results
derivative <- function(f, x, h) (f(x + h) - f(x - h)) / (2 * h)
parallel <- function(curve_name) closed$curve_sensitivity |> filter(curve == curve_name) |> summarise(value = sum(npv_per_bp)) |> pull(value)
baseline_name <- "QuantLib blackFormula"
fd_name <- "QuantLib blackFormula, finite difference"
domestic_shift <- function(r) baseline_npv(discount = r)
foreign_shift <- function(r) baseline_npv(foreign = r)
bind_rows(
  compare_values("NPV", "yen", baseline_npv(), closed$summary$npv, baseline_name),
  compare_values("NPV", "percent of notional", 100 * baseline_npv() / terms$notional, 100 * closed$summary$npv / terms$notional, baseline_name),
  compare_values("FX delta", "yen per yen of spot", derivative(\(s) baseline_npv(spot = s), terms$spot, 1e-3), closed$summary$fx_delta, fd_name),
  compare_values("FX vega", "yen per percent", baseline_vega() * 0.01, closed$summary$fx_vega * 0.01, "Black vega formula in R"),
  compare_values("Domestic curve, parallel", "yen per bp", derivative(domestic_shift, domestic_curve_rate, 1e-6) * 1e-4, parallel("domestic"), fd_name),
  compare_values("Foreign curve, parallel", "yen per bp", derivative(foreign_shift, foreign_curve_rate, 1e-6) * 1e-4, parallel("foreign"), fd_name)
) |>
  show_results()
```

## Scenarios of the legacy text

```{r}
#| label: scenarios
spots <- terms$spot * c(0.90, 0.95, 1.05, 1.10)
volatilities <- c(0.05, 0.075, 0.125, 0.15)
bind_rows(
  compare_values(sprintf("Spot %.4f", spots), "yen", map_dbl(spots, \(s) baseline_npv(spot = s)), map_dbl(spots, \(s) riemann_note(spot = s)$summary$npv), baseline_name),
  compare_values(sprintf("Volatility %.3f", volatilities), "yen", map_dbl(volatilities, \(v) baseline_npv(volatility = v)), map_dbl(volatilities, \(v) riemann_note(volatility = v)$summary$npv), baseline_name)
) |>
  show_results()
```

## Monte Carlo on the same note

The legacy text uses 300 paths with QuantLib's generator through GaussQuant. Random numbers differ, so these rows are not judged. The note gives the distance from the closed form in standard errors.

```{r}
#| label: monte-carlo
paths <- 1e5
mc <- riemann_note(paths = paths, seed = 123, threads = 4L)$summary
mc_one <- riemann_note(paths = paths, seed = 123, threads = 1L)$summary
bind_rows(
  not_comparable(
    "NPV, Monte Carlo against the closed form", "yen", baseline_npv(), mc$npv,
    sprintf("%.0f paths; %.2f standard errors from the closed form; standard error %.0f yen", paths, (mc$npv - baseline_npv()) / mc$standard_error, mc$standard_error),
    baseline_name
  ),
  compare_values("NPV on 1 and on 4 threads", "yen", mc_one$npv, mc$npv, "RiemannFinMath itself")
) |>
  show_results()
```

## Five-year note with automatic differentiation

The inputs are those of the legacy text's `torch` chapter, which rates each year with its own forward rate. The side is `torch`, which is C++ and not QuantLib. RiemannFinMath's curves have calendar node dates and `torch` has whole years, and the random numbers differ, so nothing here is judged.

```{r}
#| label: torch-inputs
legacy <- lagrange_objects("part3_enterprise_riemann/ch07_prdc_autodiff.qmd", c("tbl_prdc_curve", "prdc_price_torch"), n_steps = 5L)
curve_table <- legacy$tbl_prdc_curve
knitr::kable(curve_table, digits = 4, caption = "Rates of each year")
note <- list(notional = 1e8, spot = 150, reference_fx = 150, fixed_coupon = 0.02, leverage = 0.8, cap = 0.08, volatility = 0.12, paths = 20000L, seed = 1234L)
show_inputs(note)
```

`torch`:

```{r}
#| label: torch-call
library(torch)
torch_manual_seed(note$seed)
z <- torch_randn(c(note$paths, nrow(curve_table)))
spot_t <- torch_tensor(note$spot, requires_grad = TRUE)
jpy_t <- torch_tensor(curve_table$jpy_rate, requires_grad = TRUE)
foreign_t <- torch_tensor(curve_table$foreign_rate, requires_grad = TRUE)
volatility_t <- torch_tensor(note$volatility, requires_grad = TRUE)
torch_npv <- legacy$prdc_price_torch(
  fx_spot = spot_t, jpy_curve = jpy_t, foreign_curve = foreign_t, fx_vol = volatility_t, z = z,
  notional = torch_tensor(note$notional), reference_fx = torch_tensor(note$reference_fx),
  fixed_coupon = torch_tensor(note$fixed_coupon), leverage = torch_tensor(note$leverage),
  coupon_cap = torch_tensor(note$cap), dt = torch_ones(nrow(curve_table))
)
torch_gradients <- autograd_grad(torch_npv, list(spot_t, jpy_t, foreign_t, volatility_t))
```

RiemannFinMath, with zero rates that average the yearly rates:

```{r}
#| label: torch-riemann
tenors <- paste0(curve_table$year, "Y")
jpy_zero <- cumsum(curve_table$jpy_rate) / curve_table$year
foreign_zero <- cumsum(curve_table$foreign_rate) / curve_table$year
jpy_curve <- fitted_curve("2026-01-05", jpy_zero, tenors, index = "tonar")
foreign_five <- fitted_curve("2026-01-05", foreign_zero, tenors, index = "sofr")
subtraction <- note$leverage - note$fixed_coupon
five_closed <- RiemannFinMath::prdc_value(note$spot, note$volatility, jpy_curve, foreign_five, curve_table$year, rep(1, nrow(curve_table)), note$reference_fx, note$leverage, subtraction, 0, note$cap, notional = note$notional)
five_mc <- RiemannFinMath::prdc_value(note$spot, note$volatility, jpy_curve, foreign_five, curve_table$year, rep(1, nrow(curve_table)), note$reference_fx, note$leverage, subtraction, 0, note$cap, notional = note$notional, paths = note$paths, seed = note$seed)
```

```{r}
#| label: torch-results
reason <- "Different random numbers and different times of the curve nodes"
sum_of <- function(x, name) x$curve_sensitivity |> filter(curve == name) |> summarise(value = sum(npv_per_bp)) |> pull(value)
bind_rows(
  not_comparable("NPV, closed form", "yen", torch_npv$item(), five_closed$summary$npv, reason, "torch"),
  not_comparable("NPV, Monte Carlo", "yen", torch_npv$item(), five_mc$summary$npv, sprintf("%s; standard error of RiemannFinMath %.0f yen", reason, five_mc$summary$standard_error), "torch"),
  not_comparable("FX delta", "yen per yen of spot", torch_gradients[[1]]$item(), five_mc$summary$fx_delta, reason, "torch"),
  not_comparable("FX vega", "yen per percent", torch_gradients[[4]]$item() * 0.01, five_mc$summary$fx_vega * 0.01, reason, "torch"),
  not_comparable("JPY curve, total", "yen per bp", sum(as.numeric(torch_gradients[[2]])) * 1e-4, sum_of(five_mc, "domestic"), "Different risk factors: a yearly forward rate against a node's zero rate", "torch"),
  not_comparable("Foreign curve, total", "yen per bp", sum(as.numeric(torch_gradients[[3]])) * 1e-4, sum_of(five_mc, "foreign"), "Different risk factors: a yearly forward rate against a node's zero rate", "torch")
) |>
  show_results()
```

## Against LagrangeFinance

**No row of this chapter can be judged against the legacy text.** Its values are Monte Carlo estimates: 300 paths for the NPV and 100 for the scenarios. So they appear with RiemannFinMath's closed form and without a verdict. The rows above against `blackFormula` are the reference for the closed form.

```{r}
#| label: lagrange
sampling <- sprintf("The legacy value is a Monte Carlo estimate; its standard error is %.0f yen with 300 paths", lagrange_value("prdc.standard_error"))
spot_cases <- tribble(~scenario, ~factor, "spot_minus_10", 0.90, "spot_minus_5", 0.95, "base", 1, "spot_plus_5", 1.05, "spot_plus_10", 1.10)
volatility_cases <- tribble(~scenario, ~volatility, "vol_5pct", 0.05, "vol_7_5pct", 0.075, "base", 0.10, "vol_12_5pct", 0.125, "vol_15pct", 0.15)
bind_rows(
  lagrange_not_comparable("NPV", "yen", "prdc.npv", closed$summary$npv, sampling),
  lagrange_not_comparable(paste("Spot,", spot_cases$scenario), "yen", paste0("prdc.spot.", spot_cases$scenario), map_dbl(spot_cases$factor, \(f) riemann_note(spot = terms$spot * f)$summary$npv), "Monte Carlo estimate with 100 paths"),
  lagrange_not_comparable(paste("Volatility,", volatility_cases$scenario), "yen", paste0("prdc.volatility.", volatility_cases$scenario), map_dbl(volatility_cases$volatility, \(v) riemann_note(volatility = v)$summary$npv), "Monte Carlo estimate with 100 paths")
) |>
  show_results()
```

## Differences of wrapper and core

```{r}
#| label: design
tribble(
  ~Layer,    ~Aspect,       ~`Baseline (QuantLib, GaussQuant, torch)`,                       ~RiemannFinMath,
  "Wrapper", "Instrument",  "No instrument; formula or `GaussQuant` functions in R",         "One call with the terms",
  "Wrapper", "Curves",      "Flat handles, or a vector of yearly rates",                     "OIS curve values; flat ones must be fitted",
  "Wrapper", "Schedule",    "`Schedule` and date vectors",                                   "Times and accruals as numbers",
  "Core",    "Closed form", "Not provided",                                                  "Floor plus call spread on each coupon",
  "Core",    "Monte Carlo", "QuantLib generators, or tensors in `torch`",                    "Rust threads; the result depends on the seed and not on the threads",
  "Core",    "Derivatives", "Reverse mode in `torch`; none in QuantLib's R binding",         "Reverse mode, without `torch`",
  "Core",    "Discounting", "A separate discount curve in GaussQuant",                       "The domestic curve only"
) |>
  show_design()
```
